basics.name: Louie Slocombe
basics.summary: I use computational chemistry, physics and machine learning to understand molecular systems, from quantum effects in DNA to the origins of biochemistry. At the University of Birmingham, my research focuses on AI and machine learning for sustainable polymers, with a particular interest in predicting biodegradability.
basics.label: Computational physicist & theoretical chemist

work.name: University of Birmingham
work.position: Group Leader Research Fellow in Computational Chemistry and AI/ML for Sustainable Polymers
work.summary: Computational chemistry and AI/ML for sustainable polymers, with a focus on predicting biodegradability. Supervisor: David Scanlon.
work.department: School of Chemistry · Scanlon Materials Theory Group

work.name: Arizona State University
work.position: Research Lab Manager and Postdoctoral Researcher
work.summary: Machine learning, chemical complexity and graph theory applied to the origins of biochemistry, chemical space exploration and protein folding. Supervisor: Sara Walker.
highlights: Developed physics- and chemistry-informed models and databases using PyTorch, scikit-learn and ESMFold, alongside molecular dynamics, quantum chemistry and machine-learning interatomic potentials for polymers, proteins and DNA/RNA.

Made a substantial contribution to a funded $1.5 million NASA ROSES grant: developed the Science and Technical Management section, prepared Facilities & Equipment and Open Science Data Management Plan sections, and drafted the budget. Planned and delivered two-thirds of the grant workload.
Mentored, supervised and trained four postdocs, one staff scientist, 12 graduate students and four undergraduates, and supported new group members through onboarding.
Managed day-to-day research operations, identified training needs, and led weekly interdisciplinary meetings, workshops, research seminars and a journal club.

Organised two two-day annual lab retreats, including career development and team-building activities. Taught and guest lectured in the School of Earth and Space Exploration and the School of Complex Adaptive Systems.
work.department: Beyond Center for Fundamental Concepts in Science

work.name: University of Surrey
work.position: Research Fellow in Theoretical Quantum Biology
work.summary: Open quantum systems, non-Born–Oppenheimer effects, DNA damage, ion-channel transport, catalytic surfaces and material systems. Supervisor: Marco Sacchi.
highlights: Mentored and trained three graduate and four undergraduate students. As primary supervisor for two MPhys research students, supported projects that each produced a paper and earned a grade in the top 5% of the cohort.
Trained researchers in programming, HPC, ab initio methods, DFT, machine-learning potentials, molecular dynamics, QM/MM, minimum-energy paths, enhanced sampling and free-energy calculations.
Taught and guest lectured in chemistry and physics, and delivered outreach talks and mentoring for aspiring scientists.

work.name: University of Surrey
work.position: Postgraduate Researcher, Teaching Assistant, and Outreach Volunteer
work.summary: Computational chemistry and physics applied to biology, focusing on proton transfer and DNA replication fidelity.
highlights: Performed ab initio quantum chemistry calculations using national computing facilities including ARCHER, ARCHER2 and DIRAC.
Worked as a teaching assistant and laboratory demonstrator, teaching, grading and training undergraduates.
Created a cross-faculty initiative to improve computing support and code literacy for PhD students while serving as a physics and chemistry student representative.
Contributed to science outreach through demonstrations, talks and mentoring schemes.

work.name: University of Wollongong
work.position: Masters Research Student, Student Demonstrator, Teaching Assistant, and Outreach Volunteer
work.summary: Ultrafast terahertz spectroscopy and imaging, computational signal extraction and specialist electronics.
highlights: Developed hardware control and automation for robotic systems.
Published a first-author paper from undergraduate research.
Co-founded the University of Wollongong Astronomy Society and contributed to teaching and outreach.

work.name: Fourth State Medicine
work.summary: Research and development at a biomedical start-up developing atmospheric plasma technology for advanced wound care.
highlights: Led development of atmospheric plasma technologies from proof of concept through to commercialisation.
Designed and executed studies that provided foundational data for a patent application.
Developed microcontroller-based systems for automated experimental data acquisition and analysis.
Managed quality assurance testing and validation to meet ISO 13485 medical-device certification requirements.
